Thank you for making this course freely available! It's a good introduction to a variety of ML algorithms/ topics by a leader in the field. Mr. Ng was a large part of the reason I was inspired to tread the ML path. I will however not be paying for this course unless someone expects to see it on a resume.The course is unpolished. Errors are rampant in the code provided, to the point where you'll spend just as long figuring out the nuanced bugs in the starter code as making your own. Notation is often confused between implementation and theory, where matrices must be inverted to make the code work properly. Video segments repeat where Andrew states things incorrectly. Video quizzes are often at the wrong time-stamp, so they sometimes quiz before they teach the info. After spending hours on yet another excruciating exercise session, it's honestly getting to the point where I'd rather look up a sampling of other people's solutions and figure out what's going on that way. I care about learning, not struggling (although I understand sometimes they are one and the same). I am not finding as much value in the exercises as I expected because often the background tools of the exercise are glossed over. I'll probably return to these exercises once I understand things better, but for now they don't hold as much value in the context of the course.For a little extra work/ rework this could have been a great course. Instead you have chosen to patchwork fix things over the years. Considering this course is often the first one most everyone turns to as an introductory ML course, it would be well worth the effort to clean things up. That all said. I would like to thank you again for taking so much time and making this course available to someone like me who works a regular day job on top of studying in the evening. In the end, I feel the real value in this course was sharing insight about how to prioritize and not waste your own time when developing ML applications. This was an excellent introduction!

Overall, the course is very good. Positives: Great introduction to machine learning if you've previously never studied itCovers core machine learning ideas, algorithms and terminologyBeyond covering the core ideas it teaches you how to do machine learning well - avoid common pitfalls, speed up your algorithms, find the most beneficial problems to tackleI definitely feel I could take on my own machine learning project from beginning to end, based on what I've learned in this course. The course is well organised and well paced so it's comfortable to get through without getting lost. Warnings:The course was more of a time commitment than I was expecting. Keeping up with the weeks is 5-6 hours per week, which is almost adding another work day. In the first 3 months that I was registered I completed 5 lessons. I only completed the whole course by doing a binge where I completed 7 weeks in 6 days. From other friends experiences doing a binge was the only way they got through Coursera courses as well. If you are not familiar with statistics or programming I think you will have to cover a lot of outside material just to read all the mathematical notation and do the basic programming exercises. Although I manage to pass the exercises every week I'm not sure how much of the material is necessarily well embedded in my brain, rather than I just learned it for 24 hours. I think the additional exercises where Coursera has you right up your own summary of a lesson is an effective aid for retaining the material, but those didn't come up often. I would encourage Coursera to have more of those or make them part of the weekly assignments.

Content is good but a bit dated.  Rectified Linear Units should probably be used for activation functions.  That is a relatively small detail, however.  Probably more time would be spent if done today on streaming analytics.  Some time is spent on MapReduce.  Spark should at least get some treatment.  One of my biggest gripes is that the quizzes appear to be written by someone other than Dr. Ng.  Often there is stuff in the quizzes not covered in the lecture material.  I am a full time programmer and have been for many years, and I understand vetorization as used in APL, R, and MATLAB, so the programming assignments were very good for someone of my programming level.  I could concentrate on the machine learning techniques and not struggle as much with the language as I see some people do in the forums.  Overall, I learned a lot.  I really wanted that certificate and the quiz on Recommender Systems/Collaborative filtering should really be re-worked.  I failed it the first 3 attempts.  Then re-listened to the lectures taking detailed notes.  Failed another 3 times.  So this final time I got 5 out of 5 but had to think outside the box on a couple of the questions.  My recommendation (pun intended) is that you re-work those questions for that quiz.  Most of the others I passed first time through.  Again, overall, I learned a lot and would recommend this course to others.  Its not for the faint of heart.  I would tell anyone to brush up on their Linear Algebra (I kinda did it in parallel) before taking the course.

As an introductory course into machine learning, this was an *excellent* course.  I would HIGHLY recommend it.  The videos and the accompanying programming exercises went very well together; and the free license to Matlab for this course was great (thanks, MathWorks)!A few downsides:  some of the programming exercises (esp. the latter ones) were quite trivial, and should have gone deeper. Much of the code was provided for the user. For example, the SVM lab focused on very basic programming that only required VERY few lines of vectorized code, while completely missing opportunities like exploring tuning the performance by deciding how many features to down select to.While Dr. Ng suggested that students who have completed the course are now "experts" in machine learning (an encouraging statement, but far from reality), it would be more constructive to recommend next courses and/or books to read.Lastly, it would have been REALLY REALLY nice if Dr. Ng had written a book with all of this course content.  Other books I've read just don't have the same breadth, content & guidance. The slides/notes simply do not capture all of the material that he shared; and, it's not convenient to rewatch the videos as a replacement for a book.  Walking away from this course I don't have any effective resources to turn to in order to revisit the material that was presented.

Great course. Happens to be my first exposure to knowledge machine learning (never read any book or tutorial prior to this). I loved several aspects of the course, such as: The logical sequencing and building up of concepts, the use of problem-case to introduce each algorithm, the frequent switching over between math and real-world, the constant attention to tiny formulaic detail and rigor while still maintaining an easy-flowing conversation. I also perceived some areas of improvement (which I mention hesitatingly, as I'm very new to the field): (1) Should do more to sharpen student's skill in tying a high-level real-world problem description to a catalogged ML problem (2) Need to provide help in understanding why the student's answer on a Quiz question was wrong. (3)  I felt there was some crucial gap in the course material on NN that hit me hard while doing the programming task for back-propagation (4) A basic intro to NLP would have been great for someone like me who is at zero on the subject. (5) I was left wondering what the term "Deep Learning" meant, and where it fits, vis-a-vis ML. (6) For each of ML algorithm introduced, it would have been great if it ended with a clear statement of what concepts would be already implemented in off-the-shelf libraries, and what concept would remain to be judiciously applied / implemented by us.

Introduction to Machine Learning is an excellent course. It has helped me grasp the basic concepts of machine learning, which looked quite alien to me before this. Andrew Ng is an amazing teacher. The structure of the course is unique, as it focuses on application of learnt concepts, which is, in my opinion the biggest requirement for any educational resource. So not only do I know these concepts now, but also I am confident enough to apply them in real world problems. The programming assignments are very well designed as they contain all the code in an understandable format, and cover all the taught topics very well. You can view the provided codes for an even deeper understanding of how things work and can take your understanding to a new level.|The only problem I have with the course is that it feels very boring. I don't know if its the content that's boring or the way that it is expressed, but I didn't feel like spending most of the time of my day learning through this course although I had the time, as I didn't feel like it. I hope that this course would somehow become more entertaining and involving in the near future.Thank You Andrew!

Overall I feel the depth of the information and difficulty of the assignments is well balanced for a free online course. With barely any high level math knowledge I was able to complete the course fairly quickly. Even though the notation was sometimes hard for me to read and decipher. I appreciated the explanations in text form a lot (the lecture notes and the programming tutorials). They really helped tie the whole thing together. Sometimes hints in the pdfs for the exercises would confuse me rather than help me.I think professor Ng is a good teacher. Pleasant to listen to. The explanations in most of the video were fairly easy to understand. Going over graphs and visualizing what was going on was really helpful in understanding the algorithms.I really like the practical tips as well, where it was explained how to analyze performance of an algorithm and what can be done to improve it based on clear metrics.Thanks to all those involved for creating this course. I feel I understand a lot more than I did before I started but I also know this is just the tip of the iceberg.

Great class, focusing a lot on "intuition" about the algorithms and teaching how to get a "feeling" for the -- often quite complex -- input structures, like matrices and vectors. The programming exercises make the problems plastic and understandable. As a physics major (who had no problems with the math) I enjoyed that the focus was completely on use cases and concrete examples and not on theoretical problems, like maybe convergence criteria, possible exceptions of rules, etc.What I would criticise is that the course sometimes makes the impression that not all slides are perfectly up to date. The examples are often quite old. And while they still are perfectly delivering the message, I would prefer at least some connection to today's fast-moving developments in ML.As someone who is new in the field it was great to see how you can get quick results in Octave/MATLAB, but some examples that use TensorFlow (with e.g. python) would have been really nice as well.All in all an interesting and entertaining course from which I learned a lot!

Excellent course in machine learning. Reviews key methods and applications, and gives both concepts, application examples, as well as actual programming exercises to understand how to actually build such machine learning systems. The discussion groups and tutorials are helpful, and the mentors (Tom Mosche in particular!) are very active in helping students when they are stuck...without giving away the answers. My only comment is that i did this course with basically no programming experience, and the learning curve on the programming portion was pretty steep, even if we didn't have to program all the code, just some critical parts of it. I would either make it clearer that you need programming experience (on Matlab or Octave) as a prerequisite, or include more optional tutorials on programming, use of loops, etc...). But overall very glad i took it i have a much better understanding now of how regression, neural networks, PCA, recommendation engines, etc...works. Thank you!

Thoroughly enjoyed this course - it was my first Coursera course.  I have a degree in Pure Maths and IT, but I graduated back in 1995 so it's over 20 years since I did anything academic.  This brought so much back and introduced me to ML which is absolutely fascinating and I intend to study more on ML e.g. try some of the dataset problems on Kaggle.  I did this course purely for recreation and got through it in just over a month (I work full-time).  I liked that I could work at my own pace and get ahead so that if other commitments took over, I could put it aside for awhile and still be on track. I have knocked off one start because: I would have liked more practice questions/exercises to cement some things (it was easy to forget what some of the variables stood for in some of the longer equations;  the audio quality was not great.  That said, I realise that this was the first MOOC from Coursera, so I expect that's been improved in other courses since.

Overall, highly recommend this course to anyone who wants to get a good understanding and hands-on experience with Machine Learning principles, algorithms, implementation, and best practices.  If you have a background/familiarity with Linear Algebra and Probability, it makes it easier to follow and understand the sessions but the material that is relevant is covered so not a big deal if you don't. The mentors on the forum are super helpful with programming exercises.  The programming exercises had a whole lot of boiler plate already coded so that the student can focus on the ML parts of the exercises which improves the learning experience.  The one suggestion for improving the course and reducing student confusion would be to make the notation and methodology used in the lectures and programming exercises to be more consistent.  Some of the description of the exercises help/guides (in the pdf) were more complicated than they needed to be.

Fantastic course. Helped me get from zero technical knowledge of machine learning all the way to the point where I feel comfortable implementing and can think through those implementations. The course itself is very math-intensive and gives a deep technical understanding of machine learning, rather than just a code-based approach. I feel like this is useful, but I would not recommend this course to people with no coding experience or people who are uncomfortable with linear algebra (primarily matrix operations for vectorized implementations of algorithms). My only criticism is that the course moved slowly at some points, but I took time off to take the course in several days rather than over a few months. I imagine the reminders and short review of topics that have already been covered would be very useful to people taking the course at the recommended pace.

A good balance of theory and practice to get started with ML. I tend to be academic-oriented, so I often had to pause and go off reading up other sources (or other online courses) to be able to really understand the concepts in a intuitive way. On the other hand, the quick schedule and programming exercises of this course helped stay on track and pushed me forward. Octave was a fun tool to learn ML with but I imagine I will have to learn other programming languages after this course.As for time-commitments on this course, some weeks are heavier than others (esp if you want to understand the theory deeply), and on average I spent 20 hours per week. Programming exercises were easy (for me) unless I had a bug, and then debugging was hard. For those who are academic-oriented like me, I highly recommend studying Linear Algebra in advance of this course.

I like:-Short videos are better than one long lectures.-Quizzes help us understand the concepts.-Programming assignment in Octave teaches me how to implement the mathematical concepts.I don't like :-Concepts of few topics are not explained clearly.Advice:-This course tells the application of ML like spam detection, cancer detection, predicting movie rating, classifying groups using Matlab programming language.-Here focus is on implementation and moderate amount of concept explaination but everything is explained in detail.-Given the time limit of this course its not possible also.-Anybody with basic understand of linear algebra, statistics and good understanding of any high level programming is enough.-Matlab is easier than Java and C.

Solid foundational knowledge for those starting in ML. I like the structure of the class overall, building up on content of previous section, and the choice of MatLab as the the language/programming environment. I'd wish there was more time spent on mathematical aspects (e.g. for PCA or backprop), but I do understand that's probably unrealistic for an online class, and the additional theory could be gained elsewhere. Good practical advice on optimizing and tuning the ML systems (e.g. week 6), though appreciating this knowledge probably takes more practical applications. Finally, I found the quiz sections in Week10/Week11 to be more cursory compared to the other weeks, and wish there were practical assignments in the last two sections.

I loved this course! The manner in which Andrew stepped through the concepts and showed how to more easily understand some of the more complex ideas really helped me stay motivated and also to grasp easily. This in turn kept me wanting to learn more. I also learned a new programming language/tool in Octave as a bonus. This course comes highly recommended by many in the industry and so the certificate is handy to have as a career move. The only slight element that is missing I feel is some of the other machine learning concepts out there like Reinforcement/Q-learning, Deep learning and how it extends Neural Networks etc. But this does not in itself undo the value that is gained from this course. Thanks Andrew and Coursera!

This is an excellent introduction to machine learning. The lecture delivery can be a little dry and sometimes devotes as much time to self-evident material as to more complex concepts that could perhaps have been discussed in more detail. However all the required information is provided and the practical exercises are extremely well structured. This seems to be helped by the selection of Octave as a learning platform as it allows very direct interaction with complex matrix mathematics. You only need a small amount of training on the language which is provided in the course and it really helps you to seek out powerfully computationally efficient solutions. Overall highly  reccomended.

A very good course and introduction to this topic overall.  The videos are perhaps a bit old and some of the material might benefit from being updated, but this is still a solid class and was very much worth my time.  It has left me interested in pursuing this topic further, and possibly consider it as a career choice sometime in the future.The programming exercises were useful for learning the material and not too difficult or time consuming, and generally the help available on the class forums was enough to get me through the few difficult parts (learning how to properly vectorize some of the problems can be difficult trying to do it on your own based only on the lectures).

This was my first online course and it was more fun than I expected it to be! Kudos to Dr. Andrew NG and his team for coming up with a great course structure, amazingly clear lecture videos and fun programming assignments.  It was also nice to go through forums and read comments by mentors and other students and solidify your understanding of the concepts.  My only complaint is that the course could have been made more intellectually challenging by increasing the level of difficulty in the quiz questions and decreasing the hand-holding in the programming assignments.  Also, several typos towards the end of the course were a bit frustrating.  But overall learnt a great deal!

The course taught the mathematics behind most of the algorithms and now moving forward, I will not just be using some library function but will have a good understanding of what it does under the hood. Also, the parts of the course that stress on evaluation of the algorithms and areas to focus to improve accuracy, debugging and prioritizing tasks is great. I would have loved to have more programming assignments in the course. Also, the assignments include completing code with the structure already provided. Looking back, if there would have been some I needed to do entirely, I feel it would make me better equipped for further projects in this domain. Thank you!

Very good introduction into the field of machine learning, its various algorithms and use cases. Only point of criticism would be that the level is sometimes a little lower than expected. The pace of the lecture could, in my opinion, be a little faster as I found myself skipping through the videos from time to time hopping over the repetitions. Having said that, it's perfect for everyone without a mathematics background!The exercises were very good fun and very well managed through the available material, resources and the discussion forum. At the end of the course one - me anyway - wishes to go back to uni and start studying computer science.

Fantastic course! You have managed to pass on to others what you have learnt through mountains of time consuming research and experience. Your tips and tricks were brilliant. The assignments were challenging while at the same time gave a lot of help to students. My constructive criticism is possibly doing more Octave/Matlab example coding as part of your slides. As in walking through an entire exercise talking about what you would be thinking as you went through the problem and the steps you would take to complete it as efficiently as possible. Once again, great course and good luck with changing the world for the better in the future.

I would give 5 stars if the course would be done with Pandas and Python. Octave is a horrible tool. It supposed to be easy, but setting up advanced gradient optimization, creating dummy variables, using tons of functions in tons of files is just way too complicated. I wish to see model assignment solutions after the course (I know it is not realistic, but still what I've done in terms of code can be suboptimal to put it that way). The degree of math used is OK, but sometimes challenging. It's good to see all those internal aspects of the algorithms and be able to build it by yourself. It helps you be more confident.

This was a fun course.  I think I'd prefer a slight alteration to the format.  In the current form, one learns the language of the math necessary to complete the tasks which is great for an introductory course.  However, I'd love to have a directed optional longer/harder project that uses the course.  That is to say, it would be beneficial to see how to implement an entire solution to a given problem rather than just the interesting bits.  The fact that all homework is basically given to the students rather than created from scratch makes it harder to relate the lesson to what would be faced in the real world.

Very good course to understand and implement a large range of machine learning solutions. The only drawback I see here is the very poor level of mathematics contained in the course (it can be seen as an advantage for some), but less time spent on explaining basic maths and some dedicated to show the demonstrations behind the formulas would have been perfect!But apart from that, the pedagogy of the course is close to perfect, Andrew makes it really logical and easy to understand ! I have spent a great time.NB: for those who find his course too slow, I found that speeding the videos *2 is a very good solution!

The course is good as an introduction to the field of machine learning. It teaches some of the basic concepts in several ML topics and the professor gives a lot of practical advices (this is the part I found the most useful). I found it funny that professor Ng mentions several times during the lectures, that you should consider yourself an expert in the field if you finish this class, which I think is not true. If you have some background in ML, this probably isn't the course for you (or you can check it out as a refresher, it shouldn't take you much more than a week to finish the lectures and assignments).

Just about perfect. The only negative thing I can say is that I feel like the practical aspects of how to apply the ML techniques was lacking. The programming exercises were couched in terms of real-world problems, but so much of the focus was on understanding the math behind the machine learning algorithms that the details of how to setup a problem and solve it via ML were somewhat lost. With so many toolkits available today to perform the math parts of the work, it seems to me that the practical application of the techniques is more important than the math and I would have liked more focus in that area.

Machine learning is one of the most popular courses on Coursera and my friends invited me to this class. It is true that I learnt a lot from this course and Andrew Ng's teaching is vivid and insightful. However, this course needs refinement. There are so many weird repetitions in those videos and sometimes the audio is often vague. Furthermore, there are so few quiz questions and the programming assignments are too easy (just fill the formula in the blank and that's all), so students often finished a section and forgot almost everything in a month. I really hope that this course can be further improved.

Great course.  Andrew Ng can be a bit verbose at times which has required me to run his videos at 1.25x speed, but he motivates his concepts well and teaches them at a level suitable for newcomers to the subject.  The programming assignments were excellent; they enabled me to focus on just developing the algorithms and observing how they function.  However I will say I did not particularly enjoy using MATLAB (as someone from a software engineering background).  Quizzes after every topic were great and really helped to reinforce the matter and I loved having the slides to reference for later.  Great job!

The material and the lectures were wonderful. I felt like I got a lot out of this class and got a good understanding of how we could go about implementing AI systems. Only one thing I disliked in this course were the "Choose all that apply" questions in quizzes. They felt like the least useful tool to me in learning this course. It's hard to learn where you went wrong with this questions in order to learn. I would prefer if the quizzes had more questions instead of the "choose all that apply" questions. Thank you very much again! I really appreciated this opportunity to learn about machine learning!

I learned this machine learning course. This is my second course about machine learning.  Pros. [1] Mathematical backgrounds are well introduced. If their proof is quite long, the proof is omitted. [2] This course provides chance to construct major machine learning formulas using MATLAB/Octave. [3] Resources offered at last seem to be very useful to deepen my study on machine learning. I am going to use the references as a compass.Cons. [1] Audio quality is poor. As an English learner as a second language, this makes me spend more time to capture the meaning of speech. [2]

I enjoyed taking this course, from the lectures, to the quizzes, to the programming exercises; they all added more insight into understanding and implementing machine learning algorithms.  I thought the order in which the material was presented built a sound foundation for each subsequent lecture.  Professor Andrew Ng is a class act.  I thank you for offering this course on this forum.  This was the best $79 I've ever spent!I hope to make quick use of these skills that I've learned from this course in the near future.Thanks again!Take care and GOD bless!Terrence Cooke

A fantastic introductory course to Machine Learning. If you want to go from having a bit of a math and programming background to having a working knowledge of ML, this is far and away the best publicly accessible way to do it. However, if you are interested in learning the theoretical backing behind many of these Machine Learning algorithms, you should probably look elsewhere. For example, Professor Ng has excellent lecture notes and recorded lectures from his CS229 class at Stanford, which serve as a fantastic resource for advancing your ML knowledge much further.

I really enjoyed the course as this is my first interaction with machine learning (I'm a computer science graduate). But one thing that bothered me is that the course does not dig into the mathematical foundations of the topic, which I noticed is intended as the course is mainly for people in the industry. I think it would be better if there are (maybe optional) videos explaining some of the mathematics and proofs behind the theories for those who are interested in research. Nevertheless, this course most probably is the best resource to understand the topic.

Really enjoyed the class. A nicely balanced introduction to a topic I didn't know much about before. Prof Ng is very positive and engaging, and clearly has taken the time to think about how to explain the concepts in an accessible way. I would have liked more programming exercises for the last two weeks, and also some suggestions on what to do next in the final video. There are some resources to choose from hidden in the resources tab but I'm not quite sure what to do next. I guess that this is still a positive sign for the class - I'm itching for more!

The content of this course was explained so well. It is exciting material, but the delivery from Andrew Ng made it even more engaging. I am walking away from this course feeling prepped with materials and tools to actually do machine learning! My only recommendation is that the programming assignments had a little bit more variety with respect to what the student has to perform. The assignments repeat programming the cost functions or various algorithms multiple times, and although it was repetitive, I definitely won't forget how to do it.

Very nice course, thaught by one of the leaders of the field. Very practical but not enough theoretical and clearly designed for people with not that much of mathematical background (if at all) or from a software engineering/computer science background, which is frustrating sometimes when it comes to understand the underlying theory about some of the more complex learning algorithms (SVM, kernels, backpropagation algorithm). Good experience overall, i'd recommend for a very good introduction to the vast world of machine learning.

I have really enjoyed this course. I have learnt a lot. The videos are well done and present the information in an interesting way. There are some mistakes in the videos and these are highlighted in the lecture notes.The exercises are good and challenging. The discussion forums are a great resource as are the tutorials. The Ipad application had an issue where some of the diagrams and equations were displayed in a very small panel that required scrolling. Overall, a great course that covers a lot and I would really recommend.

I really enjoyed this course.  I believe it gives a great basic understanding of what machine learning is and how you can use it.  I feel that the  programming assignments could be broken up a little better to assess each section the way the PDF suggests to submit the results.  Or at least give an option to bail out of the code if you know you haven't completed the other sections.  Overall, I am very satisfied with the information provided and the instructor's teaching style.  I look forward to learning more on Coursera.

This course is a very good introduction to machine learning staff. At first half of the course, it contains basic knowledge about machine learning. The second half pays more attention on application, especially advice on real implementation. I would like to stress that doing coding homework is a perfect path to get familiar about course materials. Hope everyone who choose this course gain a lot.Last but not least, a great thank for Andrew Ng to build this platform helping everyone. Hope this course helps more people.

A good introductory course that isn't too  heavy on math. Programming assignments are pretty easy too. I'd enjoy the course more if the math were more involved.  At the very least, this course will give you a qualitative understanding of the basics of machine learning. The (ungraded) additional resources are great if you like getting into the details of what you're learning and you'll learn much more if you read them. You'll probably finish this course in a couple of weeks if you're accustomed to college level math.

I learned a lot from this course! I was glad I took time to watch all of the videos and learn the assignments. For the quizzes, I wish that there were descriptions of why you got each individual question wrong so that I would be able to learn my my mistakes make. Also, although the community was a great help for completing the homework assignments, I believe the instructions initially given and the steps given by the pdf made it extremely difficult to figure out what step was to be completed in each function.

I found the assignments to be sometimes confusing (i read the description of a question, thought i was supposed to answer several steps at once, only to realise that the tasks would be broken down in muc more detail later). Once i figured out the style, it was much easier, and i would be sure to read entire assignment first. Additionally, i sometimes didnt know whether errata notes were relevant to the code i was actually using, or previous offerings of the same course. Overall though, very good! Thanks!

A nice introductory course with broad coverage. Not sure how good for a complete beginner; with a MSc in Statistics and PhD in Economics with a heavy doze of econometrics, it was just fine. The professor is friendly and encouraging. The quizzes really test you even though they contain just multiple choice questions. The programming assignments are useful for better understanding the algorithms, although there is still some way to go before you can really apply them in the wild. Four stars easily.

The course is great and, although It has been quite challenging sometimes (since I'm a "working student") I had a lot of fun and inspiration completing it.If I have to express just ONE thing this course lacks of, is that of putting you on the right path in order to start actually working with the standard nowadays technologies available to work as a ML Engineer, but other than that, I find this course perfect for the way it teaches the theory behind whichever library you're gonna end up using.

instructor used simple theoretical examples to explain difficult ideas, while using realistic problems revealing how these methods can be applied in practical cases. Quizzes were important for keeping interest high during the lectures while programming was fun and rewarding. The submit system worked very well. Overall, congratulations for the nice presentation, the good organization of the lectures and that of programming problems and their evaluation. I should also say: it was inspiring.

The course material is great and its an awesome starting point for data analysis. However, its very unfortunate that the assignments are in Matlab / Octave. It's very important to study Python for interviews, as that is the most popular language with excellent data science tools. Also, the Octave environment is not the most stable and I often encountered problems. I wish Professor Andrew Ng had taken industry needs and data science needs into consideration while selecting the platform.

I really enjoyed the time spending on this machine learning course, however for people with engineering background and some programming experience the content is often just scratching the surface and not going as deep as you want. From my point of view it is more an introduction course of machine learning which enables you to understand the basics and arouses interests to learn more, more and more about this fascinating topic. I will continue with learning more about this technology!

The course provides deeper understanding of math and intuition behind machine learning algorithms. I felt this course is useful in getting the fundamentals if you have never taken a AI, data mining or related course . And topics such as building machine learning systems (bias vs variance trade-off), ceiling analysis are useful not only for developers and leads. I wish there should have been more sessions on real-life examples but that would be best to be covered in another course.

Amazing Course, teaches you right from basics. Prof. Ng explains everything in a manner which makes it easy to understand. Only one shortcoming I found in this course is, not challenging enough programming exercises. I understand that course has to cater a general and large crowd, but adding maybe a few optional challenging exercises might help. Also, if optional video content is provided for algorithms which have been taught in CS229 but are absent here, it will be really useful.

I liked the course for a quick summary of ML techniques with minimum prerequisites information required to understand the topics. I have previously learned most of the topics covered in more detail but from slightly different perspectives and slightly different math. I liked how this course brought those instruments I new together to application in ML.I would probably made the practical tasks slightly more complex :) Many of them were just few lines of code in vectorized form.

This course is really interesting. I recommend it especially to people with little math background, because Prof. Ng finds a way to explain the overall functioning and goal of the algorithms without relying too much on mathematics. On the contrary, if you have taken college level courses on calculus and linear algebra, as well as some probabily and statistics, some bits of the video lectures can be a bit boring. Still, an excellent course for anyone new to machine learning.

This is a fantastic course! The conceptual foundation building through intuition, graph, demos, and examples is excellent. The exercises help you solidify your understanding of ML techniques. You really get good skills and ML expertise by taking this course. The only thing this course is missing is an update to the exercises to use some of the more recent ML libraries that are gaining popularity within the industry instead of MATLAB/Octave: NumPy, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.

I very much enjoyed the class; I feel like I learned a lot. Coming from a physics background though, I found it perhaps a bit too light on the math - though I understand that this is meant to be an introduction to students from a broad range of backgrounds. Also, I would have preferred to use Python rather than Octave just because it is a more popular language, but it did make matrix operations and vectorization of programs very simple. All in all, very good course!

A great introductory course that is designed such that you don't need a mathematical background in order to understand the concepts. Due to its attempt to maximise accessibility, most concepts are not mathematically motivated, meaning that a person serious about pursuing this as a career will need to do a subsequent course that is more mathematically rigorous. However, it does a great job of building intuition about the algorithms and is a solid base to build on.

Great introduction to machine learning, and it gets you through all the concepts, ideas and terms nicely. I feel like this course is perfect for people who manage tech teams and people who wants to take their first step into the subject. Having said that, after completing the course I don't feel like I can go and build my machine learning system and that I should learn another libraries and toolkits in order to apply what I learned in real world programming.

Extremely good overview of a large variety of Machine Learning Algorithms! The only thing that bothered me a little was that everything was done in MATLAB instead of R or Python, which is probably more natural for most people taking the course. Also, this course is rather directed at people with a programming background that want to get into stats, not so much for people with a stats background that want to get into the programming part of ML (which I was).

I just finished the course and I want to say it is pretty details and covers a huge variety of topics in machine learning. The problems I had with this course is specifically with the quizzes and programming assignments; I would get stuck with no idea of what the correct way is to solve it, what I'm doing wrong, or sometimes I don't even know what the question wants me to do. However, with perseverance, I was able to get through every one of them.

Amazing starter course on Machine Learning that does an outstanding job at explaining base concepts and applications, as well as diving into more advanced subjects.It does however need some updates, as navigating through the various resources to find eventual errors in the lecture here and there is a bit counter-intuitive. Textual lecture notes that can be found in earlier weeks are very useful and I wish there were available for every week.

The course is nice as an introductory course to ML and set the path to learn more in the field. Many algorithms are not covered in much detail and programming assignments are also limited in terms of completexity and innovation. I think it all depends on the learner to really take skills from this couse and start applying them outside of the course to real problems, join tougher courses and dive deep into the algorithms taught in the course.

Andrew Ng does a very good job of stepping students through the various technologies. The programming assignments are challenging without being impossible, and relate to the subject matter at hand. His pace is good in most places, although occasionally it was difficult to following the thread of logic that brought us to various conclusions. All in all it was a good class that was immediately applicable for me in my career.

Very informative if you want to know the finer details about how Machine Learning works. If you'd rather use ML applications and not get into the math, you might want to skip over this. If however you want to know exactly why ML does what it does, this is an excellent course.I only gave 4 stars because it's also several years old. If they went back and updated and cleaned it up, it would definitely be worth 5 stars.

I really like the course and Professor Ng makes the subject approachable and easy to understand. However the Quiz Questions with "check all that apply" responses always trump me and I get less than 20% complete. These "check all that apply" questions really discourage me from going on because I feel inadequate 'stupid'  and have to constantly check my work rather than demonstrate any mastery of the subject.

Very good overview of machine learning. Doesn't go into detailed mathematical construction of the methods/techniques but the course does provide you with the overall/big ideas used in machine learning.  If you are completely new to machine learning, definitely take this course! If you're from a different background (math/stat etc), this course will provide you with a good transition into machine learning.

A great course really. I learned easily many things about the field while I had no prior knowledge (but I had a good programming knowledge). The course is well taughts, introduces many concepts and provides good foundation to understand the concepts and learn even beyond the course if you want to. My only critic: it misses some info about the most recent developments around neural networks.

The course is really great to understand machine learning from scratch! Videos are really instructive and the many quizzes and exercices are well thought.  The only (small) inconvenient is that sometimes the learner spend a lot of times explaining some basic concepts making the video a little long. Still, I highly recommend this class to anyone who wants to learn about machine learning!

Great course! Provides an excellent understanding of the possibilities of machine learning and key details to choose the correct analysis/project design. Only frustrating thing is that programming assignments can be quite frustrating in a way that isn't really furthering your understanding of machine learning. Of course, this is probably mostly due to the nature of programming.

This is a very easy to understand and well informative course with very good examples for each of the topics. The best part is you get to see a few very interesting cases where machine learning just hits the bull's eye, which keeps you motivated throughout the course. Overall, the course is neither too mathematical nor too much formula based, it has a good balance between two.

Prof. Ng presented an excellent machine learning introductory course, covering various topics that are the necessary foundation. Without getting into too much mathematical details, Prof. Ng managed to convey many machine learning ideas in a clear way and all the programming exercises are very well design for learning those skills. Thank you so much for making this course!

Would have been great if there was a final capstone project where students actually need to try out different models, tweaking parameters etc..and finally zeroing in on one model, without them being given any assistance which was not the case in programming exercises . This could have been added at the end at-least as an optional exercise if not as a graded one.

Extremely helpful course. Especially that it shows ways to test and tune the own work and to find out, what to put effort on. I missed some more on clustering, eg how to measure the quality of a clustering. I know that there're some KPI's but after the class I still cannot interpret them. So one less star and I hope that you add this little thing to the course.

This course offers a very clear path towards understanding machine learning.  By the end of the course I understood high-level ML concepts and am now well-equipped to begin learning further.  I only say 4/5 because there are some glitches in the course around the timing of the in-video quizzes, and some of the videos need to be edited.  Otherwise fantastic!

Course is great. Andrew Ng is an incredible teacher, and makes understanding the concepts really straightforward.Some small cons:Programming assignments could be larger;Language used in the course could be Python instead of Matlab - would be more usefulOverall, essential course for everyone wanting to get started in the exciting field of Machine Learning.

First class that I took at Coursera and first introduction to this field of Machine Learning.Nice narrator, good overview of several topics. Very nice problems to fix our understanding.Only negative side: For a master graduate in science/engineering, it is maybe to informal. More mathematical formalism and explanations would maybe be more interesting.
reviewers: By Carlos M d C T

reviews: Terrific instructor, easy to follow and well paced. Covers a lot of area but the exercises are very much hand holding where your part is just plugging in a few lines of code. I've been doing modeling work for many years and this machine learning course has given me additional tools that I feel will definitely be helpful for solving future problems.

Great introductory course to the field of machine learning.At the same time, if you already have some strong knowledge of linear algebra and/or probability theory, I would like to recommend the other version of this course (also thought by Andrew Ng), which is more advanced and can be found for free here https://see.stanford.edu/Course/CS229

A good introductory course, but there are two issues:1. The programming exercises are a bit dumbed down (you mostly fill in code fragments rather than write everything from scratch, which could make you miss a few points about how it all works).2. Professor Ng at the end tells you that "now you are expert in machine learning". This is a lie.

Loved this course.Using MATLAB for matrix calculations made work easier.Programming assignments and quizzes highlighted areas which I needed to work on so I found them helpful.Last but not the least,loved Prof.Ng 's style of teaching and also am grateful to Tom and other mentors for keeping up with questions I and other students had.

This machine learning course is the first course of my acquaintance as a layman, curriculum content is easy to understand, very suitable for such 0 basic courses, but the content of these courses are a lot less than the network course of Standford, hope to supplement the corresponding content, to satisfy my curiosity for learning.

Great course for those eyeing for a quick know-how. Wouldnt recommend it to those particularly interested in learning the mathematics behind the algorithms. Prof Ng is undoubtedly a great teacher, makes the concepts look simple and easy to understand. In short, I d rate 5/5 as an engineer and 4/5 as someone interested in the math.

Very good course. I don't know if there could be updates performed since it dates back to 2011 and I imagine that there might be some new stuff in the field since then (maybe a short introduction to deep learning?) Some corrections should be applied to some materials. Last courses do not include summaries as the first ones.

good course for diving into machine learning. Amazing teacher, good learning resources everything is explained in a very understandable way, complicated concepts were made easy by Prof. Andrew.application of the algorithms not touched to the level i was expecting but all in all a very good course for people diving into ML.

Great introduction to Machine Learning. Altough it is not intended for people that has strong mathematical or algorithmical background, Andrew NG reaches explain in a very detailed way many concepts of ML.I suggest this course to people that face ML for the first time, not to people that only want to deepen his knownledge.

The course definitely enhanced my knowledge about the subject to a greater level and inspired me big time to get into the core of the subject and start working on the implementation of the tools and algorithms in real life applications. It would have even better if more of  practical applications are dealt with the course.

Very good course.Would be better if the differences between Logistic Regression and SVM were clarified; they seem identical to me.Also, it wasn't clear to me that Linear/Logistic Regression was formulated as Batch Gradient Decent (ie each step uses all examples) until later, when Stochastic Gradient Decent was introduced.

Very simple and mathematically unsophisticated (which could be a good or bad thing depending on your background) but well-organised and a generally worthwhile introduction. I'd recommend watching the videos sped up to 1.5x or 2x if you're comfortable with the mathematics since the pace of the videos is otherwise too slow.

Overall very good, however this youtube video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aircAruvnKk by 3Blue1Brown on Neural Networks made some features about neural networks at lot clearer. Specifically, in understanding what the hidden layers actually do. Including a similar introductory video to that topic would have helped me.

The Course was very nice the teaching of Mr. Andrew were nice and very understanding. The course has done great help to me by bringing me one step closer to my dream. The assignments were challenging and enjoyable. Also thanks to coursera for providing the certificate on scholarship. It was nice to be part of the course.

A well-planned course, going step by step into some of the finest ideas in machine learning. Assuming low mathematical and computational foundation, it provides a technical path for learners to acquire needed tools of building a machine learning system, while successfully dealing with the inadequacy of precise analysis.

Great, just some of the assignments are a bit frustrating simply because you aren't given clear instructions on what you are supposed to do.  Getting assistance with code is also near impossible for some questions.  Overall I learned a lot and enjoyed the class, but there is still a bit of room for improvement I think.

The course is very interesting and Andrew Ng is a great teacher.It 'a shame for the bad audio (too much compression?), as well as for quizzes and programming activities that are often too trivial.However I recommend this course at those who want to explore these fascinating themes and at those who want deepen a little.

An excellent class!  Very effectively builds the fundamentals of machine learning for persons with no prior background in ML.  But if you already have some background in ML and are looking for a comprehensive review of state of the art machine learning techniques in 2017, this is probably not the right class for you.

I absolutely loved this course. The one thing I feel that could be improved upon is building up these algorithms from scratch rather than filling in functions as part of the programming exercises. We should learn to plot the data and read in files into our program on our own. Other than that, excellent course.

Andrew is hero of ML. This course was great as pretty comprehensive understanding of ML methods. My only gripe is that the course spends way too much time repeating the mathematical aspect of the algorithms and misses out on practical introduction to how one can start employing ML after finishing this course.

Would have liked examples in the finance/economic space. Also, perhaps greater discussions about how we can decide on the appropriateness of the number of hidden layers and nodes for Neural nets. Otherwise it gave me a great breadth of knowledge to go try and apply for loan level modeling techniques.

Good course overall but it loses a star because the assignment instructions are rather complicated, confusing and in a few cases send students completely in the wrong direction.  Thankfully Tom Mosher has posted "Tutorials" (under Resources) that honour the vectorized approach shown in the lectures.

A really excellent course for practical implementation of various algorithm. This will suit users who are not seeking a deep mathematical understanding of these topics, even thought Andrew tries to show the general idea for a lot of the concepts. Overall a great course, and good coding practice! :-)

One of the best courses I have reviewed and certainly I enjoyed completing the programming exercises. For the lectures though I have gone through Prof. Ng's original Stanford lectures in greater details. It gives anybody without any ML experience a very nice overview of the algorithm and practices.

Great content, great slides, good examples.However, even though Dr. Ng takes time to explain the fundamental concepts and length and repeats multiple times, when it comes to complex topics, he glances over them. I ended up referring to external (Dr. Hinton, for instance) for deeper understanding.

Personally I didn´t have experience about ML. The course is didactic and helps to understand lots of concepts. Nevertheless, I strongly suggest to improve scripts since there are some issues to upload homeworks and even there is an answer within the forums, should be a good idea to fix this.

Topics covered in the course is excellent. As a person working in the industry this would be more helpful if some other programming language like python or r is used instead of octave for assignments.Apart from that the course is awesome. We will get deep understanding of machine learning.

This course provides an excellent introduction to machine learning and some good coding practice. However, there were many times I wrote code that successfully solved the desired problem, but had to rely on the tutorials and totally rewrite code that was not accepted by the grader program.

A great introduction to machine learning mathematics and concepts.  Andrew does a great job making most of the topics accessible.  My only complaints are:  (1) the videos are old and contain errors; and (2) some of the quiz questions require multiple answers and are not crafted very well.

Great Class! I hope you can develop a 2nd part to this course that goes more into the theory and advanced concepts of machine learning however I'm really fortunate to have learned from you since you were able to explain everything in such a simple and accessible manner. Thank You Andrew!

This course has been a great learning experience and I have learned a lot. One more suggestion I want to recommend is that there should have been more involved in the derivation of some of the techniques. Those videos can be optional for those who are more into the mathematical stuff.

Great course delineating all the fundamental principles. Some parts of it maybe a bit too easy for people with decent linear algebra knowledge but definitely a comprehensive and worthwhile introduction in the exciting topic of Machine Learning. I'm definitely motivated to learn more !

This course is a great course. I appreciate the efforts of professor and other teaching assistants to make things easier to understand. It will be great if Professor explains how to create data sets in real life (probably in some additional videos). Thank You for such a great course.

This was a great intro into Machine Learning. My only complaint is that it was very heavy in mathematical theory. While that is a necessity for the industry, I would have liked to see more examples of practical applications and implementations with modern technologies and libraries.

Andrew Ng well respected in the field. Lectures take clock time, & test are more of tests than learn along, though the field is a recipe today not analytic too. Some intuitive insight on distributions and cost y log h -(1-y) log(1-h)  can help. SVM, Back forward prop are in here.

Congratulations for the course! I really liked to learn all the topics about machine learning, but unfortunately it could have more topics like deep neural networks and Knowledge Discovery in Databases(KDD). Besides this, the course could accept code submissions on R language.

Teaches you concepts of regression, basics to start of with Machine Learning. Assignments could be slightly modified and applied to many real life problems. If one can find a real time project, and apply the concepts they learn from this course they can make total use of it.

This course provided me with a good overview of various Machine Learning concepts and technique. However, I do feel that it would be much better if there are more optional videos on mathematical detail as I sometimes feel groundless when those math details are slopped away.

Pretty good intro course for machine learning. My few minor gripes are the use of MATLAB/Octave (poor translation into industry) and a lot of the course materials have not aged well (i.e. the video really need to be re-recorded - primarily to fix the poor audio quality).

the course itself is great, but it lacks quite a bit to perfection, simply because the professor made mistakes (which is totally normal), but it wouldn't have been too much effort to correct them ... :/one has to read up in the course wikipedia about all the typos etc.

Five minus one star for quality of the video and general lack of programming assignment practical help. Those are minor concerns considering the wealth of knowledge, wisdom actually, and passion that Andrew Ng brings to this course few other instructors could provide.

Well organised, good practical exercises. I think it could be a good idea to use python as an alternative to make the programming exercises, as the "scaffoldings" for each one are really well prepared for the student, and it's only necessary to write a few code lines.

There are many new examples using ML recently, 30 minutes session on the latest examples by 2017 should help us and excite us more. Also how ML can be used in other technologies like Data Science and others also could help us in building our career in right direction

Very good. Only downside : tries too much to be understandable to everyone no matter its mathematical background. So that Eventually for those with deep background in math, the lesson is very often confusing because of the lack of a clear mathematical model behind.

Great overview to
get you started on ML. Very cool exercises in Octave. Even if you - like I - really not care to learn Octave, I strongly recommend  spending time on these.The last 2 weeks are a bit vague, but also very fast to complete.Thanks for a great course.

great lectures, thanks andrew.  i particularly liked you silicon valley insights! sometimes the exercises were so tough, that even I with a phd in econometrics struggled... the risk is to loose a lot of time on matlab syntax... but we had great support by tom...

I would have liked the course to be more customised to an individual. More like a conversation with a private tutor and less like a one size fits all lecture. It might also be a good idea to get a games designer involved to think about how it could be more fun.

Could have done with some more theory and programming exercises could have had a little less emphasis on Vectorization. Would have been nice to implement a whole machine learning pipeline.Andrew's a great instructor though and quickly covers all the key topics.

I had problem to understand Theta uses in math formulations then now it's very clear.It is a while that I doesn't do maths like this. a real pleasure to make this course. Maybe try to plan to use Python with that course instead of Matlab.Thanks for the work !

Nice place to start for beginners in Machine learning . Will defineitely help you to grab on the theoretical concepts needed in this field . But not much of programming is involved in this course rather the focus is on the subject matter and algorithms.:)

While I had som familiarity with the concepts from before, I would sincerely recommend this course to anyone who wishes to learn how to implement machine learning. Do not however that the course expects a lot from you in terms of mathematical knowledge.

I very beautifully designed courseAndrew Ng has done a great job at making these videos as easy to understand as possibleAlthough I feel there is bit of interesting factor lacking from the course which is causing most people to leave the course mid way

The pacing of this course is extremely well refined.  The content moves along at a speed that just allows you to keep track.  It's a little overwhelming at times, but as this course has been around for a while there's plenty of help available in the

I've learnt a lot of machine learning through this course and I've realized how machine learning systems work actually. Especially, the part of supervised learning was very detail. However, I thought that unsupervised learning could be more detail.

Good coverage of every topic, very helpful for passionate students like me. The instructor is very knowledgeable about machine learning career. The standard of this course is good. The explanation of examples and problems is good overall. Thank you

It is the best course any beginner can find in the field of Machine Learning. It starts with the most basic concepts and gradually teaches some very important aspects of the field.The only con is that the quality of video and sound is bad at times.

In some places the course was a bit lengthy, but on the whole it was interesting and very well structured.With this course I was able to immerse myself even more deeply in the subject area of machine learning.Thanks a lot Prof. Ng for this course!

Fantastic topic, even for people not directly working in programming.I'm in marketing and wanted to know more about the possibilities behind this specialty. The course is definitely challenging but manageable with some efforts, and worth doing it.

I have to say the programming part can be elaborated in a clearer way for beginners. It took me really a hard time to find my own way out. It might be part of the fun for learning, but it's also dangerous to keep some people away from continuing.

Great introduction to machine learning and the complex topics surrounding it.  Some of the programming assignments are extremely challenging but the class is very worth while, persevere through the more difficult assignments, it'll be worth it.

Some quiz questions and parts of the programming assignments seem a bit arbitrary, but the course is solid overall. I'd strongly advise making heavy use of the tutorials and test cases for the programming assignments in the resources section.

Great at giving a fundamental, necessary understanding of machine learning. The quiz system drove me crazy--not as helpful at reinforcing understanding. Big value is in the programming assignments--helped much more to reinforce understanding.

This is a great course for the beginners of machine learning and artificial intelligence. The contents are quite comprehensive and inspiring. The most important is that all the assignments are delicate and well-designed.  Highly recommend!!!

Easy to understand and very good for beginners in the field. But AFAIK it lacks of current state 'what's the exact classificators, which are used at present in subareas (it could constantly change though) and lacks of deep learning overview

The assignments are too time consuming but the challenge helps learning. I would suggest more assignments with more hints and help specially when it gets to intricacies of linear algebra and octave coding which is quite time consuming.

Good overview of machine learning concepts, but most of my effort int he programming exercises went toward fiddling with Octave, rather than really gaining more practice with, or a deeper understanding of the machine learning concepts.

Great for an intuitive and practical introduction to machine learning, however the theory is left behind, which may be bothersome to some (it was to me anyhow). However, Mr. Ng really couldn't be clearer about what he discussed here !

It's a bit outdated  now, I think. Plus, his lectures that are available in YouTube are way more challenging/fascinating. Looking forward to his latest AI course though.Nothing can take away the fact that he is an amazing teacher.

Phenomenal course, I found myself transported back to my college studies which I enjoyed very much. Would have been cool if there was a video introducing topics not talked about in this course such as RNNs and such. Thank you Sir!

Fantastic beginning and middle, but after Week 7 the programming homework gets absurdly easy and you do less of the nitty gritty and more just listen to Andrew give you tactical advice. It's useful, but I didn't enjoy it as much.

This is an excellent course explaining the material very clear. The programming-assignments are very helpful to deepen the knowledge.I deduct one star only because the videos could be sometimes have a better technical quality.

Basic concepts of machine learning are developed in a clear and easy-to-follow manner, but the practice of eschewing mathematical derivations may lead to occasional confusions. Also, the programming assignments are trivial.
